newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Space monkeys return to earth, said feeling fine.
newsitem.headline: Space monkeys return to earth, said feeling fine.

text.p: Lapik and Multik, two monkeys who spent 14 days in space as part of a Russian-U.S. research project, landed in Kazakhastan on Tuesday and were said to be "feeling fine".
Television pictures showed the Bion-11 craft Earth on a snowy field on Kazakhstan's border with Russia shortly after it came down to Earth as Orthodox Christmas Day dawned across Russia.

"Two minutes after it came down, helicopters carrying Russian and American specialists landed nearby and we got to work," said Vladimir Khakhov, a specialist with the Federal Aviation and Cosmic Search and Rescue Service.
"The flight was successful and the "cosmonauts" Lapik and Multik are feeling fine," he told Reuters.

One of the two specially bred macaque monkeys was shown looking dazed as the scientists, who placed a tent over their capsule to protect it from the freezing temperatures, opened up the craft and stroked its arm.
Tests were begun immediately and the two monkeys were later flown to Moscow for further study.
Lapik and Multik, strapped into the capsule with monitoring equipment around their heads, were trained to carry out a series of tasks in space on commands given by ground control.
"If they did them quickly and correctly, special, tasty food was fed through a feeding tube," said Khakhov.
Their mission in space cost $30 million, half of it put up by the U.S. space agency NASA, said Russian space officials.
Animal rights groups in the United States protested against the experiment, the latest in a research programme begun by the Soviet Union in 1973. The next Bion flight is due next year.

France, Ukraine and Lithuania also took part in Bion-11, which scientists say will provide evidence of the effects of weightlessness on animals and plants that have not been prepared for space travel. The data will help in planning manned flights.
"One can't do such experiments with people, but they are very important for long flights to Mars etc as significant changes occur throughout the organism," said Khakhov.
